title: dir2mcp_open_media_clip
description: Extract and return the audio/video snippet for a media hit (SPEC §15.11). Time-media analogue of dir2mcp_open_file: returns media bytes for a time span rather than transcript text.

chunk_id.description: Hit chunk id; resolved to its source media and time span.

max_bytes.description: Optional caller ceiling on the CLIP bytes (not the response). The effective bound is min(max_bytes, media.clip.max_bytes). The server MAY re-encode to a reduced-fidelity preview to fit under it, and MUST say so via the output preview field; when even a preview cannot fit the span under the effective bound, CLIP_TOO_LARGE.

data.description: Required when return=inline (see allOf below): base64 clip bytes. content[] carries the SAME clip in addition, in the item SPEC 15.11 names for the media kind (audio: a native audio item; video: an embedded resource whose resource carries blob plus a video/* mimeType, because MCP 2025-11-25 defines no video item). So an inline response holds the clip twice, and media.clip.max_bytes bounds the CLIP rather than the response.

uri.description: Present when return=reference: short-lived fetch URI.

expires_unix.description: Present when return=reference: expiry of uri.

reference_fallback.description: Present ONLY when the caller asked for return=reference and the server served inline instead; explains why. Its PRESENCE is the signal that the returned return value is not the one asked for, so a caller tests presence and does not parse the text. Absent whenever the requested carrier was honoured.

preview.description: Present ONLY when the served bytes are a reduced-fidelity re-encode rather than a source-fidelity cut; names the rendition for a human (codec, resolution, approximate bitrate). Its PRESENCE is the signal that the clip is a preview, so a caller tests presence and does not parse the text. Absent whenever the bytes are cut at source fidelity.
